subject: Critical Thinking
title: Moving the Goalposts: When Nothing Will Satisfy
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Moving the Goalposts: When Nothing Will Satisfy.

hook.text: 'Show me evidence.' You do. 'That's not the right kind of evidence.' You show more.

buildup.text: Moving the goalposts: continuously changing the criteria for proof so that no evidence ever satisfies the demand.

discovery.text: It's a dishonest debate tactic that makes the person APPEAR to value evidence while actually being immune to it.

twist.text: Counter-strategy: before presenting evidence, ask 'What would it take to change your mind?' Pin down the goalposts.

climax.text: If they can't name any evidence that would change their mind, they're not reasoning — they're defending a fixed belief.

punchline.text: If no evidence could change their mind, it was never about evidence.

quiz.question: What is the best counter to someone who moves the goalposts?
options: Ask them to specify what evidence would change their mind before you present any

details.summary: Moving the goalposts means changing the criteria for proof after evidence has been provided. It makes arguments impossible to win because the standard keeps shifting.
details.whyItMatters: Recognizing goalpost-moving prevents you from wasting energy meeting endlessly changing demands and exposes bad-faith debating.
takeaways: Shifting criteria after evidence arrives is intellectually dishonest
Pin down criteria before presenting evidence
Goalpost-moving is a sign of bad-faith engagement

faq.question: How do you counter someone who keeps moving the goalposts?
faq.answer: Establish clear criteria for what would count as proof before the debate begins. When the opponent shifts, point to the agreed standard and ask them to explain why it changed.

faq.question: Is moving the goalposts always intentional or can it be accidental?
faq.answer: It can be unconscious. People sometimes raise the bar reflexively when confronted with unwelcome evidence. Pointing it out politely helps distinguish honest updating from deliberate evasion.
